headline: Britain says it will keep early access to the most powerful US AI models for safety testing, after reports that the White House had tried to limit it.
score_reason: Lowered from 6 to 5: the minister's speech was on Monday 12 Oct, a day before the window, and it confirms a change we already carried from a newspaper report.
importance_line: People relying on independent safety checks of the strongest AI models keep a UK government test before release, but the minister's own warning that breaches are likely shows testing does not remove the risk, and the US side of the change is known only from media reports.
summary: AFP reports that Kanishka Narayan, the UK's AI minister, confirmed in a London speech on Monday 12 Oct 2026 that Britain's AI Security Institute, the government body that tests advanced models, keeps early access to the most powerful AI models before release, which AFP calls a reversal of the Trump administration's reported request to OpenAI and Anthropic that our 12 Oct 2026 edition carried from the Telegraph, as relayed by Reuters. Narayan said the institute now has access to Google's most powerful model, Gemini 4 Argon, which AFP says had not been released publicly, and warned that it is "likely, if not inevitable" that Britain's own cyber defences will be breached.
notes: AFP full text read. Speech was Monday 12 Oct 2026 (Japan Today carried the AFP story that evening), so the event is older than the window start; score lowered one point. Continues the 12 Oct 2026 edition item 26 (Telegraph via Reuters). Gemini 4 Argon was launched publicly on 13 Oct per The Verge, after the speech.
